title: A Painless Way to Measure the Eye

patient.name: Mdm Lee Geok Hoon
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for optical coherence biometry before left eye cataract surgery

history.hpc: Mdm Lee has a visually significant cortical cataract in her left eye that has been gradually worsening over the past year, causing glare while driving at night. She has been listed for left eye phacoemulsification with IOL implantation. The doctor has ordered optical coherence biometry (IOLMaster or equivalent) to calculate the IOL power, as her cornea is clear enough for the non-contact method. She has never had this test before and is slightly anxious about a 'machine touching her eye'.
history.pmhx: Cataract left eye (cortical). Mild cataract right eye, not yet visually significant. No previous eye surgery. Mild hyperopia.
history.family_hx: Sister had cataract surgery in her 60s
history.social_hx: Retired teacher. Lives alone. Still drives during the day.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right eye: early cortical lens changes. Left eye: moderate cortical cataract, clear cornea.
examination_findings.fundus: Right eye: normal. Left eye: hazy view due to cataract but no obvious posterior pathology

optical_biometry.signal_quality: Good signal-to-noise ratio bilaterally, no measurement excluded

diagnosis: Optical coherence biometry completed successfully on both eyes via non-contact method. Left eye axial length, keratometry, anterior chamber depth, and white-to-white obtained with good signal quality. IOL power calculated for surgeon review for left eye phacoemulsification.

immediate: Confirm correct patient identity and confirm left eye is the surgical eye to be measured
Explain the procedure to patient: non-contact, no anaesthetic drops needed, patient just looks at a fixation light
Ask patient to remove contact lenses if worn (not applicable here, but check routinely)
Set up the optical biometer and enter patient details accurately into the system
Position patient comfortably with chin on chinrest and forehead against the rest, instruct to blink normally then keep eyes open and fixate on the target
Capture measurements for both eyes — axial length, keratometry, anterior chamber depth, white-to-white
Check signal quality indicator for each measurement; repeat any scan with poor signal
Take repeated measurements until consistent readings obtained, then select the best set
Print report including IOL power calculation and hand to doctor / upload to patient record
follow_up: Surgeon to review biometry results and confirm IOL power and formula
If signal quality remains poor due to dense cataract, contact (immersion) A-scan may be required as backup
Biometry data filed in pre-operative record
patient_education: Reassure patient that the machine does not touch the eye
Explain the test takes about 5-10 minutes and is painless
Tell patient that this measurement helps choose the correct lens implant for her surgery

key_points: Confirms correct patient identity and confirms which eye is the surgical eye
Asks about contact lens wear (soft lenses removed at least 1 week, RGP 2 weeks before accurate keratometry)
Asks about previous eye surgery, which can affect axial length and IOL calculation
Explains the non-contact nature of the test to reduce patient anxiety
Sets up optical biometer correctly and enters patient data accurately
Positions patient correctly at chinrest and obtains good fixation
Checks signal quality for each measurement and repeats poor-quality scans
Records axial length, keratometry (K1/K2), anterior chamber depth, white-to-white, and IOL power
Identifies that optical biometry is non-contact and generally preferred over A-scan when cornea is clear enough
Recognises that dense cataract may cause poor signal quality requiring contact A-scan as backup
Identifies the purpose: IOL power calculation for cataract surgery
Does not proceed with incorrect patient identity or wrong eye
Documents all biometry parameters accurately and completely
Hands printed report to surgeon or uploads to records
Educates patient on the painless, non-contact nature of the test
Recognises when to escalate to contact A-scan if signal quality is inadequate
